methods.topic: one specific company, person, or event studied in depth
methods.guideDescription: An in-depth look at one person, group, or situation in its real-world setting.

methods.topic: reactions to a product, idea, or design before launch
methods.guideDescription: A guided discussion with a small group to learn opinions, reactions, and ideas.

methods.topic: personal stories, experiences, or expert opinions
methods.guideDescription: One-on-one conversations that explore personal experiences in depth.

methods.topic: measurable opinions or habits from a large number of people
methods.guideDescription: A standard set of questions given to many people to measure trends in numbers.

methods.topic: answers hidden in existing records, reports, or archives
methods.guideDescription: Studying existing records, texts, and data to find patterns or history.

researchers.name: Maya Chen
researchers.bio: Maya is the life of every lab meeting. She can get a room full of strangers talking within five minutes, and arguing within ten.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Chen will help clients who want to test reactions to a product or idea before launching it.

researchers.name: Sofia Rossi
researchers.bio: Sofia thinks the best conversations happen with a clipboard and a snack table. Her focus groups have a waiting list.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Rossi will help clients who need honest reactions to a new design, logo, or advertisement.

researchers.name: Priya Nair
researchers.bio: Priya loves a good spreadsheet. If it can be counted, she has already counted it twice and color-coded the results.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Nair will help clients who want to measure what a large number of people think or do.

researchers.name: Miguel Morales
researchers.bio: Miguel is a model citizen, regular lab-meeting attendee, and all around swell guy. In fact, the only bad thing about him is that no one can think of anything bad to say about him.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Morales will help clients who need to track habits and opinions across a whole campus or town.

researchers.name: Dev Patel
researchers.bio: Dev drinks too much coffee and has never met a question he couldn't turn into a three-hour conversation. Somehow, people leave happier.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Patel will help clients who need expert opinions from people with years of experience.

researchers.name: Marcus Lee
researchers.bio: Marcus is a natural listener who remembers everyone's name, and their dog's name, and what the dog is allergic to.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Lee will help clients who want to understand personal experiences, like why someone made a big life choice.

researchers.name: Hana Tanaka
researchers.bio: Hana once spent an entire summer studying a single coffee shop. She still knows the barista's favorite song.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Tanaka will help clients who want to understand why one particular business or event succeeded or failed.

researchers.name: Omar Haddad
researchers.bio: Omar believes every problem is a story with a beginning, a middle, and a suspiciously long appendix.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Haddad will help clients who need a close look at one person, team, or community and how it works.

researchers.name: Charles Ville
researchers.bio: Charles Ville isn't afraid to pick a fight with a bad dataset. He specializes in digging through dusty archives, old reports, and forgotten footnotes.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Ville will help clients whose answers are hidden in old reports, records, or archives.

researchers.name: Elena Novak
researchers.bio: Elena once found a missing grant report in a 1987 filing cabinet and has been insufferable about it ever since.
researchers.specialtyBlurb: Novak will help clients who want to know how something has changed over time, using records that already exist.
